This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed seeking an order to set aside the judgment dated 07/10/2009 in MCOP No.331 of 2017 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (District Court), Karur.

sentences.text:
2.The facts in brief:-
On 18/10/2016 at about 10.20 pm, when the deceased Sivakumar was riding a two wheeler bearing registration No.TN-47AH-4080 along with his father as pillion rider on the Karur-Trichy main road, when he was nearing the occurrence place, a Lorry bearing registration No.TN-29- AB-2360 was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner in the opposite direction coming on the wring side of the road and hit the two wheeler.

As a result of which, both were thrown out of the vehicle,
Sivakumar died on the spot.
The first petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

3.The deceased Sivakumar completed Diploma in Mechanical Engineering and working as a Mechanic in Sundaram Linings Ltd., Chennai and also undergoing B.Tech (Mechanical Engineering) Course at that time.
Claiming compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/-, the claim petition was filed by the dependents.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

4.That was resisted by the Appellant Insurance Company by filing counter stating that the Insured vehicle did not involve in the occurrence and it was falsely implicated in this case; Other customary denials were made.
Apart from that, it is also stated that the Lorry driver was not having proper driving licence.
5.Before the Tribunal, on the side of the claimants, two witnesses were examined and 12 documents marked.
On the side of the Insurance Company, 3 witnesses were examined and 4 documents marked.

6.At the conclusion of the enquiry process, the Tribunal recorded a finding on the point of negligence that it occurred due to the lorry driver bearing registration No.TN-29-AV-2360 and its involvement was also verified and confirmed.
7.Regarding the compensation
, the age of the deceased was fixed at 24 years.

Considering the fact that he was a Diploma holder in Mechanical Engineering and was working as part time employee in a private concern, the monthly income was fixed at Rs.8,028/- and to that, 50% towards future prospects was added.
50% was deducted towards personal expenses.

So it arrived at Rs.6,021/-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis per month as Loss of Income.
By adopting multiplier method by taking 18 as multiplicand, it arrived at Loss of Income at Rs.13,00,536/- and other conventional heads were also added as noted below:-

Total compensation awarded Rs.14,60,536.00 8.Against which, this appeal is preferred by the appellant.
9.Heard both sides.
10.The learned counsel appearing for the appellant would submit that the involvement of the vehicle bearing registration No.TN-29-AV-2360 was not established before the Tribunal.
He also reiterating the counter averments.
11.Now let us go to the evidence of RW1 on this aspect as extracted by the Tribunal in its order.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
12.The
4th respondent herein/RW1 is the driver of the offending vehicle.
According to him, for loading the goods, he started driving the vehicle from Mayanur, midway he found some crowd and later, was informed that load was not available.
So he returned back to his house.
But however, a false case has been registered against him.
According to him, his vehicle was not involved in the occurrence.
13.From his evidence, it was ascertained that during the relevant time, he drove the vehicle through Mayanur and crossed the Toll Plaza.
It is also verified from the CCTV footage available in the Toll Plaza.
It is also informed that within 15 minutes from the occurrence, he received information that a case has been registered through phone.
During the course of investigation, the involvement of the vehicle was identified and final report was filed before the trial court.

From the police investigation,
the Tribunal concluded that only the vehicle bearing registration No.TN-29-AV-2360 was involved in the occurrence.
14.The learned counsel appearing for the appellant would rely upon Toll Plaza Time Ledger, which reads that it crossed the Toll plaza at about 10.26 am on https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 18/12/2016.
So, I find absolutely no reason to differ from the conclusion reached by the Tribunal.
15.The Investigating Officer is the best person to verify the involvement of the vehicle.
As mentioned above, it was found out during the course of the investigation.

So, that can be taken as a concrete proof for the involvement of the vehicle bearing registration No.TN-29-AV-2360.
16.Except the oral evidence of RW1, no other acceptable evidence has been let in by the Insurance Company to show that it was not involved in the occurrence.
Simply because, RW1 drove the vehicle after making the accident without stopping, his involvement cannot be doubted.
RW1 cannot take advantage of his own wrong.
Why he is referring to the crowd and in the midway also creates suspicion of the involvement in the occurrence.
So, I find that correct conclusion was reached by the Tribunal, which requires no interference at all.

, with regard to the compensation, no argument was advanced by the appellant.

19.The
age of the deceased was fixed at 24.
As per his Transfer Certificate, he was admitted in the first year B.Tech Course at Chennai.
Before that, he completed Diploma in Mechanical Engineering and was getting a monthly salary of Rs.8,026/- lastly.
That was taken into account.
50% was added towards future prospects.
50% amount was deducted towards personal expenses.
Finally the Loss of Income was calculated at Rs.13,00,536/-.
To that, conventional amounts were added as detailed below.
Loss of future income Rs.13,00,536.00  Loss of consortium Rs. 1,20,000.00  Loss of estate Rs. 15,000.0  Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000.0  Transport expenses Rs. 10,000.0

Total compensation awarded Rs.14,60,536.00  20.The calculation of Loss of Income   conventional heads are just and reasonabl  requires no interference.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 21.In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
